sets.ref: hand: 100 MB = 100 x 10^6 B x 8 = 8e8 bit (NIST: 1 MB = 10^6 B, 1 B = 8 bit); 8e8 bit / 1e8 bit/s = 8 s; no framing: net rate = line rate, efficiency 1

hand (independent script): 8N1 = 1 start + 8 data + 1 stop = 10 bit per 8 data bits (TI SPRUGP1 data format; Microchip: 'a typical USART frame has 10 bits'); t = 8388608 bit x 10/8 / 115200 = 91.0222 s; cross-check via the net rate: 115200 x 8/10 = 92160 bit/s, 8388608 / 92160 = 91.0222 s
hand (independent script): 1 MB = 8e6 bit; t = 8e6 x 10/8 / 115200 = 86.8056 s, 4.86 % shorter than 1 MiB (ratio 1.048576)
published: Microchip USART brief: 8N1 transmits BAUD_RATE/10 characters per second: 9600 Bd gives 960 characters = 960 B = 7680 bit in 1 s; net rate 9600 x 8/10 = 7680 bit/s

hand (independent script): 8E1 or 8N2 = 11 bit per 8 data bits (TI SPRUGP1: start + data + optional parity + stop bits); t = 8388608 x 11/8 / 115200 = 100.1244 s; net rate 115200 x 8/11 = 83781.8 bit/s, efficiency 8/11 = 72.7 %
hand (independent script): 1 MB = 8e6 bit; t = 8e6 x 11/8 / 9600 = 1145.833 s; net rate 9600 x 8/11 = 6981.82 bit/s
